In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the electron and heavy-hole dynamics in GaSb-based QW heterostructures.
the carrier capture dynamics in GaSb-based QW heterostructures.
the development of a new class of semiconductor lasers, which are capable of emitting in the 2-3 μm wavelength region.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the carrier dynamics in GaSb-based QWs with different QW widths is governed by the QW carrier confinement energy.
the carrier capture dynamics in type-II QW structures is determined by the QW confinement energies and the barrier carrier relaxation rate.
the electron and hole relaxation dynamics is determined by the QW confinement potential.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that type-II QWs in GaSb-based structures are very efficient for carrier capture and relaxation, and that the electron and hole confinement energies can be controlled by changing the QW design.
the electron-hole recombination rate in type II quantum wells is limited by the hole capture from the barrier.
we have demonstrated the first type-II QW lasers with high efficiency and high power.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the carrier relaxation in QWs is not instantaneous and the electron and hole capture times are different.
the carrier dynamics in type-II heterostructures can be controlled via the QW barrier thickness.
the carrier capture time is a function of carrier confinement energy in the QW, which allows us to control the carrier capture rate and, therefore, the threshold current density in type-II QW lasers.
